 Florida reclaims top spot in Andy Katz's men's basketball Power 44 rankings after Week 2
 Every single shot from Darius Acuff Jr.'s 2026 March Madness run with Arkansas 
 Share 
 Florida retook the No. 1 spot in Andy Katz's Power 44 rankings after Week 2 of men's basketball, knocking Duke to No. 5.
 Here are the full rankings from his latest Power 44:
 Florida (2): Back at No. 1 after a one-week absence. Took care of another in-state rival in Florida State.
 UConn (4): The Huskies are title good, and proved it with another Power 4 win — this time over Ohio State. 
 Michigan State (5): The Spartans beat back Duke behind another stellar performance from Jeremy Fears Jr.
 Kansas (10): The Jayhawks had a dominating performance over Kentucky in Chicago. 
 Duke (1): No shame in the Blue Devils losing to Michigan State, but a number of tests are upcoming against UConn and Florida. 
 UCLA (6): The Bruins are rolling the competition in Westwood. 
 Vanderbilt (7): Love the Commodores' backcourt of Ace Glass and Tyler Tanner, which could end up being the best scoring duo in the SEC. 
 Arizona (11) : The Wildcats got their first big-time Power 4 win by winning at Auburn. 
 Texas Tech (19): The Red Raiders outlasted Illinois in Lubbock for their first significant win of the season. 
 Houston (12): The Cougars are back to holding teams under 70 points a game. 
 Illinois (3): The Illini fans may be a little salty, but the reality is the Illini aren’t healthy yet, so it’s hard to fully judge this squad against the top 10. 
 Texas (14): The Longhorns got a rivalry win over former conference foe Baylor in San Antonio. 
 Virginia (9): The Cavs came back to beat former ACC rival Maryland. 
 St. John’s (15): The Red Storm continue to own Madison Square Garden with a win over Syracuse. 
 LSU (32): Look out, SEC, because the Tigers are for real after Donovan Dent’s 3-pointer beat Gonzaga in Spokane. 
 Gonzaga (13): The Bulldogs shouldn’t be dinged too much after losing to a loaded LSU at the buzzer. 
 USC (16): The Trojans have one of the best 1-2 scoring punches in Alijah Arenas and Rodney Rice. 
 Alabama (17): Amari Allen is living up to the hype in leading the Tide to a win over Seton Hall. 
 BYU (20): Rob Wright III continues to look like a first-team Big 12 player and an all-American in leading the Cougars. 
 Nebraska (21): The Huskers continue to throttle teams defensively, and this time the victim was Boise State in South Dakota.
 Memphis (25): The Tigers had a historic 18-point comeback to take down Louisville by 20! 
 Louisville (8): The Cardinals collapsed in the second half in Memphis, and that should serve as a needed early-season wake-up call. 
 Miami (Fla.) (18): Remember the name Brent Bland, who came off the bench to score 26 points in 20 points with eight 3s in a win over North Alabama. 
 Arkansas (22): The Hogs are taking care of the teams they should beat, thus far, but will get another major test this week against Indiana. 
 Tennessee (23): The Vols will find out where they stand when they host Michigan State this week. 
 Michigan (26): The Wolverines took care of Marquette and are finding their rhythm. 
 Georgetown (30): The Hoyas may be for real with their second power four win, this time on the road against Clemson.
 Baylor (31): The Bears came close to knocking off Texas and will be a top-tier Big 12 team. 
 Kentucky (24): The Wildcats got picked apart by Kansas and then barely survived beating NAU. But I’m not giving up just yet. Too much talent. 
 TCU (28): The Horned Frogs added a major piece with the addition of former SLU and A-10 player of the year Robbie Avila.  
 Georgia (41): The Bulldogs went in and beat North Carolina for one of the best non-conference road wins of the Mike White era. 
 Wisconsin (33): The Badgers had a 22-0 run to beat Fairfield and are finding no issues scoring this season. 
 Indiana (NR): The Hoosiers escaped with a quality W over Syracuse in Indianapolis. 
 DePaul (40): The Blue Demons may just be a real player in the Big East by winning at rival Northwestern by 20. 
 VCU (34): The Rams have just one blip, and it was a one-point loss at Memphis. 
 Minnesota (NR): The Gophers got a shelf-life true road win at the buzzer by beating Cincinnati. 
 Missouri (36): The Tigers beat a struggling Marquette in Chicago but did so without Mark Mitchell. 
 West Virginia (NR): The Mountaineers are quietly going about their business and holding teams to 61 points or less.
 Auburn (29): The Tigers will get a chance to redeem themselves after losing to Arizona by 11 with West Virginia next. 
 Ole Miss (NR): The Rebels' defense is going to be a problem for teams in the SEC. 
 High Point (NR): The Panthers had one of the most impressive wins of the week by winning by 10 at Saint Louis. 
 Notre Dame (NR): The Irish haven’t had a letdown since opening the season with a win over Villanova in Rome. 
 Xavier (NR): Richard Pitino has a squad worthy of a potential top five Big East finish with an impressive win over Mississippi State. 
 Texas A&M (NR): The Aggies are back with Buddy Ball after beating Oklahoma State by 19.
 Dropped out:  Saint Louis (27), Iowa State (35), Ohio State (37), Florida State (38), Marquette (39), New Mexico (42), Iowa (43), Grand Canyon (44).  
 Eight additional under consideration 
 Creighton
 Grand Canyon
 Utah State
 Santa Clara
 San Diego State
 Pitt
 Virginia Tech
 Rutgers
 Andy Katz is an NCAA.com correspondent. Katz worked at ESPN for 18 years as a college basketball reporter, host and anchor. He's covered every Final Four since 1992, and the sport since 1986 as a freshman at Wisconsin. He is a former president of the United States Basketball Writers Association. Katz can also be seen covering college basketball on Big Ten Network during the regular season. Follow him on Twitter at @theandykatz .
